seoTitle: Crawl Depth vs Bot Hits by URL Path Depth
metaDescription: Count crawler requests and distinct URLs by path depth to see where bot crawling thins out on your site. Free, local, no upload.
intro: Shows hits, distinct URLs and hits per URL for each path depth, with a small bar chart.
why:
Sites that bury content deep in folders tend to see fewer visits there. A table of hits by depth shows whether crawling falls off sharply at a certain level.

Depth here means the number of path segments in the URL. It is not the number of clicks from the home page, so a deep URL can still be linked from the home page. Use it as a first look, then compare with a click-depth report from a crawler.
howTo: Decide whether query strings make separate URLs.
Look for the depth where hits per URL drop.

faq.q: Is path depth the same as click depth?
faq.a: No. Click depth is the number of links from the home page. Path depth only counts folders in the URL.

faq.q: What should I do if deep URLs are rarely crawled?
faq.a: Link to them from stronger pages, add them to the sitemap and check that they are worth indexing.

faq.q: Can I trust the bot names in the result?
faq.a: Only as claims. The tool reads the user-agent text, and anyone can send a fake one. For anything that matters, check the IP addresses against the operator's published ranges or with reverse DNS.
